bio.topic: Enzymes as biological catalysts: the lock-and-key model

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is a catalyst?
options: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up
A substance that is used up to start a reaction
A substance that slows down a reaction
A product formed at the end of a reaction
questions.answer: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the catalyst at the end of the reaction.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Enzymes are biological catalysts made of which type of molecule?
questions.hint: They are long chains of amino acids folded into a shape.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What name is given to the part of an enzyme where the substrate binds?
questions.hint: It is the 'working' region of the enzyme.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What name is given to the molecule an enzyme acts on?
questions.hint: It goes into the enzyme before the reaction.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In the lock-and-key model, which part is represented by the 'lock'?
questions.hint: The key fits into it.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why does each enzyme usually catalyse only one reaction?
options: Its active site has a shape complementary to only one substrate
It can only work once before it is used up
It is too large to fit other molecules
It only works in the stomach
questions.answer: Its active site has a shape complementary to only one substrate
questions.hint: Think about shape and fit.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is formed when a substrate binds to the active site of an enzyme?
questions.hint: Its name combines the two molecules involved.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What happens to an enzyme after the products are released?
options: It is unchanged and can be used again
It is broken down into amino acids
It becomes part of the product
questions.answer: It is unchanged and can be used again
questions.hint: Remember the definition of a catalyst.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Amylase breaks down starch. What is the product of this reaction?
questions.hint: It is a sugar made of two glucose units.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which word describes the shapes of an active site and its substrate?
questions.hint: They fit together like matching puzzle pieces.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: An enzyme digests 6 g of starch in 3 minutes. Calculate the mean rate of digestion in g per minute.
questions.hint: Rate = amount ÷ time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Without a catalyst a reaction takes 240 s. With an enzyme it takes 30 s. How many times faster is the reaction with the enzyme?
questions.hint: Divide the slower time by the faster time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Protease enzymes break down proteins into:
questions.hint: Proteins are long chains of these units.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Describe the sequence of events, using the lock-and-key model, from a substrate meeting an enzyme to the release of products.
questions.hint: Use the terms substrate, active site, complex and products in order.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why lipase cannot break down starch.
questions.hint: Compare the shape of lipase's active site with the shape of starch.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Suggest why living cells need enzymes to carry out their reactions at body temperature.
questions.hint: Think about how fast reactions would be without them, and what high temperatures would do to cells.

bss.topic: Jânio Quadros, João Goulart e o golpe de 1964

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano Jânio Quadros renunciou à Presidência da República?
questions.hint: Ele ficou menos de sete meses no cargo, depois de tomar posse em janeiro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual objeto Jânio Quadros usou como símbolo de campanha, prometendo 'varrer a corrupção'?
questions.hint: É um objeto usado para limpar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem era o vice-presidente quando Jânio Quadros renunciou?
questions.hint: Era conhecido pelo apelido de Jango.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Onde estava João Goulart no momento da renúncia de Jânio?
questions.hint: Era uma viagem oficial a um país socialista da Ásia.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Que movimento, liderado a partir do Rio Grande do Sul, defendeu a posse de Jango em 1961?
questions.hint: O nome lembra o respeito à lei e à Constituição.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual solução foi adotada em 1961 para permitir a posse de Jango com poderes reduzidos?
questions.hint: Nesse sistema, o primeiro-ministro passa a ter grande parte do poder.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano um plebiscito fez o Brasil voltar ao presidencialismo?
questions.hint: Foi no início do ano seguinte ao de 1962.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como ficou conhecido o conjunto de reformas propostas por João Goulart, como a agrária e a educacional?
questions.hint: O nome indica que mexeriam na estrutura do país.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas era uma das reformas de base defendidas por Jango?
questions.hint: Tinha relação com a distribuição de terras.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O comício de 13 de março de 1964, em que Jango defendeu as reformas de base, ficou conhecido como:
questions.hint: Aconteceu em frente a uma grande estação de trem no Rio de Janeiro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual manifestação, em São Paulo, reuniu setores conservadores contra o governo Jango em março de 1964?
options: Marcha da Família com Deus pela Liberdade
questions.answer: Marcha da Família com Deus pela Liberdade
questions.hint: O nome cita família, religião e liberdade.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que contexto internacional ocorreu o golpe de 1964?
questions.hint: Disputa entre Estados Unidos e União Soviética.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem foi o primeiro presidente do regime militar após o golpe de 1964?
questions.hint: Era um marechal do Exército.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que a renúncia de Jânio Quadros gerou uma crise política em 1961.
questions.hint: Pense na reação dos militares e de setores conservadores à posse do vice.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que as reformas de base provocaram oposição de alguns grupos da sociedade?
questions.hint: Pense em quem poderia perder terras ou poder com essas mudanças e no medo do comunismo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Analise dois fatores que contribuíram para o golpe de 1964.
questions.hint: Considere fatores internos (economia, política) e externos (contexto internacional).

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is a stakeholder?
options: Any person or group with an interest in a business
Only the owners of a business
Only the customers of a business
questions.answer: Any person or group with an interest in a business
questions.hint: It is a broader group than just the people who own shares.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is an internal stakeholder?
questions.hint: Internal stakeholders work inside or own the business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is an external stakeholder?
questions.hint: External stakeholders are outside the business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What name is given to the owners of a limited company?
questions.hint: They own part of the company's shares.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the main objective of most shareholders?
options: High dividends and a rising share price
questions.answer: High dividends and a rising share price
questions.hint: Think about a return on their investment.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which objective is most likely for employees?
questions.hint: Think about what workers want from their job.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which stakeholder is most interested in the business paying its bills on time?
questions.hint: They provide materials and want to be paid for them.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which stakeholder group wants good-quality products at low prices?
questions.hint: They buy the products.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Why is the government a stakeholder in businesses?
options: Businesses pay taxes and provide jobs
questions.answer: Businesses pay taxes and provide jobs
questions.hint: Think about what the economy gains from businesses.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business wants to cut costs by reducing wages. Which stakeholders are most likely to be in conflict?
questions.hint: One group gains from higher profit, the other loses income.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A factory plans to expand and work 24 hours a day. Which stakeholder is most likely to object?
questions.hint: Think about noise, traffic and pollution.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which stakeholder lends money to a business and wants it repaid with interest?
questions.hint: These are financial institutions.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Identify one internal and one external stakeholder of a supermarket and state one objective of each.
questions.hint: Choose one group inside the business and one outside, then think about what each wants.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain why a decision to move production abroad could cause conflict between stakeholders.
questions.hint: Consider who gains from lower costs and who might lose jobs or business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain one way a business could reduce conflict between its stakeholders.
questions.hint: Think about communication, consultation or compromise.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A café owner wants to raise prices to increase profit. Discuss how this might affect two different stakeholders.
questions.hint: Consider customers and employees or shareholders, and give positive and negative effects.

chem.topic: Reacting masses, limiting reactants and percentage yield

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of carbon dioxide, CO₂. (Ar: C = 12, O = 16)
questions.hint: Add the Ar of each atom in the formula.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the Mr of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃. (Ar: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.hint: There are three oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the number of moles in 4.4 g of CO₂. (Mr = 44)
questions.hint: Moles = mass ÷ Mr.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the Mr of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄. (Ar: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)
questions.hint: Count two H, one S and four O.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calculate the mass of CaO produced from 50 g of CaCO₃. (Mr: CaCO₃ = 100, CaO = 56)
questions.hint: Find the moles of CaCO₃ first; the mole ratio is 1:1.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Calculate the mass of MgO formed from 12 g of Mg. (Ar: Mg = 24; Mr: MgO = 40)
questions.hint: The mole ratio of Mg to MgO is 2:2.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Calculate the mass of CO₂ produced when 8 g of CH₄ burns completely. (Mr: CH₄ = 16, CO₂ = 44)
questions.hint: One mole of methane gives one mole of carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. How many moles of NH₃ can be made from 6 moles of H₂ (with excess N₂)?
questions.hint: Use the ratio 3 mol H₂ : 2 mol NH₃.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What name is given to the reactant that is completely used up and limits the amount of product?
questions.hint: It 'limits' the reaction.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. 4 mol of H₂ react with 3 mol of O₂. Which reactant is limiting?
questions.hint: Work out how much O₂ is needed for 4 mol of H₂.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Fe + S → FeS. 5.6 g of Fe reacts with 4.0 g of S. Calculate the maximum mass of FeS formed. (Ar: Fe = 56, S = 32; Mr: FeS = 88)
questions.hint: Find the moles of each reactant and identify the limiting one.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. 0.2 mol of Mg is added to 0.3 mol of HCl. Calculate the number of moles of H₂ produced.
questions.hint: Check whether there is enough HCl for all the Mg.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The theoretical yield of a reaction is 20 g, but only 15 g of product is obtained. Calculate the percentage yield.
questions.hint: Percentage yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A student expected 8.0 g of product and collected 6.4 g. Calculate the percentage yield.
questions.hint: Divide what was obtained by what was expected, then multiply by 100.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Give two reasons why the percentage yield of a reaction is usually less than 100%.
questions.hint: Think about the reaction not finishing, side reactions and losses during separation.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why chemists often use one reactant in excess.
questions.hint: Think about making sure the more expensive reactant is completely used.
